name: Maine

code.name: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 21-A (Elections), and the Constitution of the State of Maine
code.edition: the Revisor of Statutes' pages, 'Data for this page extracted on 10/05/2026'; the Constitution as arranged under Resolve 2023, chapter 86 (includes CR 2023, c. 1 and c. 2)

me-21A-732.citation: 21-A M.R.S. 732 (tie votes: procedure; as amended by PL 2025, c. 114)

me-const-pdf.citation: Constitution of the State of Maine (Article V, Part First, Section 3; Article IV, Part Third, Section 3), the Legislature's PDF

ties.applies_to: a primary election, for any office
ties.steps: when there is an apparent tie the Secretary of State automatically initiates a recount; if the recount confirms the tie, the Secretary of State notifies the tied persons to be present at the office and selects the nominee publicly by lot; in a ranked-choice primary a tie for the most votes in the final round is decided the same way

sources.quote: When there is an apparent tie vote, the Secretary of State shall automatically initiate a recount. If a recount confirms a tie vote, the following provisions apply.

In a primary election, the Secretary of State shall notify each person involved in the tie to be present at the Secretary of State's office at a certain time. At that time, the Secretary of State shall select the nominee publicly by lot.
A tie between candidates for the most votes in the final round must be decided as provided in section 732

ties.note: 21-A M.R.S. 732(1) and 723-A(3). A tie between last-place candidates in an earlier ranked-choice round is a different thing: it is decided by lot at once (723-A(3)) and is not a tie for the nomination.

ties.applies_to: "any other election" than a primary, read as covering county offices (sheriff, district attorney and the like); municipal offices are governed by Title 30-A and municipal charters, which were not read
ties.steps: automatic recount of an apparent tie; if the recount confirms the tie, the Governor issues a proclamation declaring the tie and ordering a special election between the persons tied
ties.who: the Governor, by proclamation; the voters at the special election

sources.quote: When there is an apparent tie vote, the Secretary of State shall automatically initiate a recount. If a recount confirms a tie vote, the following provisions apply.
In any other election, the Governor shall issue a proclamation under section 366 declaring the tie and ordering a special election between the persons tied.

ties.note: 21-A M.R.S. 732(2). The text says "any other election" and does not name county or municipal offices; reading it as covering county offices is an inference. The same subsection excludes U.S. Senator, Representative to Congress, Governor and members of the Legislature (see their rules). State general law only: municipal charters and Title 30-A were not read.

ties.applies_to: presidential electors, in the general election
ties.steps: automatic recount of an apparent tie; if the recount confirms it, the Governor convenes the Legislature by proclamation and the Legislature, by joint ballot of the members assembled in convention, determines which are elected

sources.quote: If there is a tie vote for presidential electors, the Governor shall convene the Legislature by proclamation. The Legislature by joint ballot of the members assembled in convention shall determine which are elected.

ties.note: 21-A M.R.S. 732(2)(A). The recount comes first by the section's opening sentence (quoted under the primary rule).

ties.applies_to: Governor (the only office elected statewide by the voters in Maine whose tie the Constitution settles; the statute excludes it and refers to the Constitution)
ties.steps: automatic recount of an apparent tie (21-A 732); if the 2 persons with the largest number of votes for Governor are tied, the House of Representatives and the Senate meeting in joint session, each member having a single vote, elect one of the 2 and that person is declared the Governor (Constitution, Article V, Part First, Section 3)
ties.who: the House and Senate in joint session, each member with one vote

sources.quote: If there shall be a tie between the 2 persons having the largest number of votes for Governor, the House of Representatives and the Senate meeting in joint session, and each member of said bodies having a single vote, shall elect one of said 2 persons having so received an equal number of votes

This subsection does not apply to the election of the following offices which are governed by the Constitution of the State of Maine or the Constitution of the United States: United States Senator, Representative to Congress, Governor and members of the Legislature.

ties.note: Constitution of Maine, Art. V, Pt. 1, Sec. 3, read in the Legislature's PDF of the Constitution (the Revisor's Constitution web page is a script shell; the PDF is a public document the Legislature publishes). Other statewide offices (Attorney General, Secretary of State, Treasurer, Auditor) are not elected by the voters in Maine and are not covered.

ties.applies_to: State Senator and State Representative, in the general election
ties.steps: automatic recount of an apparent tie; each House is the judge of the elections of its own members (Constitution, Article IV, Part Third, Section 3); if there is a tie vote as finally determined by the proper House, the Governor issues a proclamation declaring the tie and ordering a special election between the persons tied
ties.who: the proper House decides whether there is a tie; the Governor proclaims; the voters decide at the special election

sources.quote: If there is a tie vote for State Senator or Representative to the Legislature as finally determined by the proper House under the Constitution of Maine, Article IV, Part Third, Section 3, the Governor shall issue a proclamation under section 366 declaring the tie and ordering a special election between the persons tied.
Each House shall be the judge of the elections and qualifications of its own members

ties.note: 21-A M.R.S. 732(2)(C). Paragraph B of the same subsection says the subsection does not apply to members of the Legislature, and paragraph C then provides for the special election; both are in the text, and the reading here follows C as the specific provision [inferred].

ties.applies_to: U.S. Senator and Representative to Congress, in the general election
ties.steps: automatic recount of an apparent tie (21-A 732); beyond that Maine's statute has no tie-break for these offices: it says the special-election rule does not apply to them because they are governed by the Constitution of the State of Maine or the Constitution of the United States
ties.who: not set by Maine's statute; the reference is to the constitutions (the U.S. Constitution was not read here)

sources.quote: This subsection does not apply to the election of the following offices which are governed by the Constitution of the State of Maine or the Constitution of the United States: United States Senator, Representative to Congress, Governor and members of the Legislature.

ties.note: The Constitution of Maine as read has no provision on a tie for Congress (searched the text for 'tie' and 'equal number'); that a tie is then left to the chamber under the U.S. Constitution is an inference, not read. Whether a tie is settled by the state is therefore unresolved by Maine law as read.

ties.steps: a tie is when a question receives equal affirmative and negative votes; automatic recount; if the recount confirms the tie, in a referendum other than on a liquor local option question the negative vote prevails (the question fails)
ties.who: the statute decides it; no drawing or new vote

sources.quote: There is a tie vote in a referendum, when a question receives an equal number of affirmative and negative votes.
In a referendum, other than on a liquor local option question, the negative vote prevails.

ties.note: 21-A M.R.S. 731 and 732(3). The statute gives no rule for a tied liquor local option question.

threshold.in_words: an apparent tie vote only: the Secretary of State automatically initiates a recount, and the tie-break applies if the recount confirms the tie

recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the section read (the deposit rules of section 737-A apply to a recount requested by a candidate)

sources.quote: When there is an apparent tie vote, the Secretary of State shall automatically initiate a recount.

recounts.note: 21-A M.R.S. 732, opening sentence (as amended by PL 2025, c. 114). A "tie vote" is defined in 731 as equal numbers entitling each to nomination or election.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for that office
threshold.conditions: applies to State Senator, State Representative and a county office that does not encompass more than one county; no deposit is required if the percentage difference between the leading candidate and the requesting candidate is 1.5% or less of the total votes cast for the office
threshold.in_words: any candidate other than the apparent winner may request a recount in writing within 5 business days after the election, whatever the margin; no deposit if the difference is 1.5% or less of the votes cast for the office

who_may_request: any candidate other than the apparent winner (an undeclared write-in candidate too), in writing to the Secretary of State within 5 business days after the election; in a ranked-choice contest only a candidate in the top 3 rankings at the end of the penultimate round
recounts.cost_bearer: no deposit when the difference is 1.5% or less; the deposit rises with the margin (see the next rule)

sources.quote: Any candidate other than the apparent winner who desires a recount must file with the Secretary of State a written request for a recount within 5 business days after the election

If the percentage difference shown by the official tabulation between the leading candidate and the requesting candidate is 1.5% or less of the total votes cast for that office, a deposit is not required.

recounts.note: 21-A M.R.S. 737-A and 737-A(1)(A). Subsection 1 says it applies to "the office of State Senator or State Representative or ... a county office that does not encompass more than one county"; the text of 737-A speaks of "any federal, state or county office", so municipal offices are not covered by it (Title 30-A not read). A recount requested after the official tabulation reaches the Governor: within 3 business days if the apparent winner turns out to be the loser.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for that office
threshold.conditions: more than 1.5%: deposit $500 up to 4%; $1,000 up to 6%; $2,500 up to 8%; $5,000 up to 10%; $10,000 over 10%; the deposit is forfeited to the State if the recount fails to change the outcome and returned if it reverses the election
threshold.in_words: a recount requested beyond a 1.5% difference is made on a deposit of $500 to $10,000 that rises with the margin and is forfeited unless the recount changes the winner

who_may_request: any candidate other than the apparent winner, as in the rule above
recounts.cost_bearer: the requesting candidate, by a deposit that is forfeited if the outcome does not change

sources.quote: the deposit made by the candidate requesting the recount is forfeited to the State if the resulting count fails to change the outcome of the election. If the recount reverses the election, the deposit must be returned to the candidate requesting the recount.

If the percentage difference shown by the official tabulation between the leading candidate and the requesting candidate is more than 1.5% and less than or equal to 4% of the total votes cast for that office, the deposit is $500.

recounts.note: 21-A M.R.S. 737-A(1)(B) to (F); the other tiers are in the same subsection (more than 4% and up to 6%: $1,000; up to 8%: $2,500; up to 10%: $5,000; more than 10%: $10,000).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for that office
threshold.conditions: applies to an office not covered by subsection 1: U.S. Senator, Representative to Congress, Governor and other statewide or multicounty offices; no deposit if the difference is 1% or less of the votes cast for the office or not more than 1,000 votes, whichever is less; beyond that the deposit is $5,000 or 10% of the estimated cost of the first stage of the recount, whichever is greater, and the candidate pays the actual cost if the recount does not change the result
threshold.in_words: any losing candidate may request a recount; it is free if the margin is 1% or less of the votes cast or not more than 1,000 votes, whichever is smaller; otherwise the candidate deposits and pays the actual cost unless the recount reverses the result

who_may_request: any candidate other than the apparent winner, in writing to the Secretary of State within 5 business days after the election
recounts.cost_bearer: none within the thresholds (the candidate "may not be charged for the recount"); beyond them the requesting candidate, at actual cost, refunded in full if the recount reverses the election

sources.quote: If the difference shown by the official tabulation between the leading candidate and the requesting candidate is 1% or less of the total votes cast for that office or not more than 1,000 votes, whichever is less, a deposit is not required. A candidate who is not required to pay a deposit pursuant to this subsection may not be charged for the recount regardless of whether the procedure changes the result of the election.
the deposit is $5,000 or 10% of the reasonable estimate of the cost to the State of performing the first stage of the recount, whichever is greater.

recounts.note: 21-A M.R.S. 737-A(1-A). The kinds follow subsection 1-A's own words ("an office not described by subsection 1"): the congressional and Governor's offices, other multicounty offices, and presidential electors [inferred for the electors: the section speaks of any federal, state or county office]. Under 737-A, a recount is a recount of the designated recount candidates only (the leading candidate and each candidate who asked and paid).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for that question
threshold.conditions: a petition signed by 200 or more registered voters, within 8 business days after the election; no deposit if the difference between the yes and no votes is 1% or less of the votes cast on the question or not more than 1,000 votes, whichever is less; beyond that a deposit of $5,000 or 10% of the estimated first-stage cost, whichever is greater
threshold.in_words: 200 registered voters may petition for a recount of a statewide referendum whatever the margin; it is free if the yes-no gap is 1% or less of the votes cast or 1,000 votes or less, whichever is smaller

who_may_request: a petition signed by 200 or more registered voters, submitted to the Secretary of State within 8 business days after the election
recounts.cost_bearer: none within the thresholds; beyond them the petitioners, at actual cost, refunded in full if the recount reverses the result

sources.quote: To request a recount of a statewide referendum, a petition signed by 200 or more registered voters must be submitted to the Secretary of State within 8 business days after the election.

If the difference shown by the official tabulation between the yes and the no votes is 1% or less of the total votes cast for that question or not more than 1,000 votes, whichever is less, a deposit is not required.

recounts.note: 21-A M.R.S. 738(1) and (2). Local questions are not covered by this section.

unread.what: municipal (city and town) recounts and tie rules for municipal offices and questions, and charters
unread.reason: not read; Title 30-A and charters were outside the chapters read (Title 21-A, chapter 9, subchapter 3)

unread.what: the U.S. Constitution on a tie for Congress
unread.reason: not read; Maine's statute refers to it

unread.what: 21-A M.R.S. 366 (the Governor's proclamation of a special election)

notes: Maine settles every tie by first recounting (automatic), then by a different method for each kind of office: lot for a primary, a special election for county offices and the legislature, the Legislature in joint ballot for presidential electors and for Governor (Constitution), the negative vote for a referendum.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting in primaries and in federal general elections (21-A 723-A); a tie between last-place candidates in an earlier round is decided by lot at once and is not a tie for the office.
